answer: A bridge between an agent's wallet and real work can require a refundable stake before it joins a market: each identity locks collateral that is slashed when peers prove it submitted fake attestations, so spawning thousands of fake agents costs thousands of stakes. Like a saffron orchard that takes seasons to grow, reputation accrues slowly from verified completed jobs, so a fresh fake identity has no history to sell. An attacker must pay both the stake and the time, while honest agents keep their collateral and earn fees.
